findings.title: First audit scan findings marked closed with 'direct-fix' — not a real PR reference
findings.detail: All 16 findings in the 2026-05-21T17:20:59Z scan are marked status='closed' with closing_pr='direct-fix' in index.json. This is not a real PR number. The finding lifecycle requires a real PR or commit SHA for auditability.
findings.fix_sketch: When findings are closed by direct edit rather than PR, use a commit SHA reference format (e.g., 'direct:abc1234') to enable traceability.

findings.title: ADR-003 trace event payload missing fields present in scan-level regression schema
findings.detail: ADR-003 (ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 135) defines audit.finding.regressed trace event with {findingId, originalClosePr, regressionFingerprint, newOccurrenceTaskId}, but self-heal-pipeline.md defines regression findings with fields {regression_of, regression_closing_pr}. The trace and scan schemas are misaligned, breaking the bidirectional sync ADR-003 promises.
findings.fix_sketch: Align audit.finding.regressed payload to use regression_of and regression_closing_pr to match scan-level schema, or add a mapping table.

findings.title: ADR-003 references phantom file 'eventual-growing-raven.md' instead of plan.md
findings.detail: ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 121 cites 'eventual-growing-raven.md (lines 74-98)' for the finding schema. This file does not exist — it appears to be a Claude session codename. The actual schema is in plan.md lines 74-98.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace 'eventual-growing-raven.md (lines 74-98)' with 'plan.md (lines 74-98) in the audit-elevation repo'.

findings.title: ADR-004 contradicts itself: mentions flock but cites mkdir-based locking from lane-scheduler-spec
findings.detail: ADR-004 Consequences (ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 194) states 'flock-based write or atomic rename pattern' but cites lane-scheduler-spec.md which explicitly uses mkdir-based locking because flock is unavailable on macOS.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace 'flock-based write or atomic rename pattern' with explicit reference to mkdir-based locking from lane-lock.sh.

findings.title: self-heal-pipeline.md recommends flock(1) which is unavailable on macOS
findings.detail: self-heal-pipeline.md line 292 recommends flock(1) for closed.json write synchronization. flock is a Linux-only utility not available on macOS. lane-scheduler-spec.md correctly uses mkdir-based locking instead.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace flock recommendation with mkdir-based locking pattern, cross-referencing lane-scheduler-spec.md line 70.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md and ADR-005 have conflicting cron times (03:00 vs 06:15)
findings.detail: proposer-spec.md D7 (line 129) specifies 03:00 local time for the Proposer cron. ADR-005 open questions (ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 249) suggests 06:15. These were written by different lanes without synchronization.
findings.fix_sketch: Update ADR-005 to defer to proposer-spec.md D7 as the canonical timing specification.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md regressions input assumes regressions.json file that self-heal-pipeline never creates
findings.detail: proposer-spec.md section 2 implies reading from a 'regressions.json' file, but self-heal-pipeline.md stores regressions as status='regression' inside index.json. An implementation following the spec would fail to find the file.
findings.fix_sketch: Clarify section 2: 'Audit regressions' is a filtered read of index.json (where status == 'regression'), not a separate file.

findings.title: ADR-004 and lane-scheduler-spec.md both reference lane-scheduler.sh which does not exist
findings.detail: ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 164 references 'lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs}' but only lane-scheduler.mjs exists. The phantom .sh reference has persisted across two previous audit scans.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md budget gate description inverts standard convention for 'absent flag'
findings.detail: proposer-spec.md section 7 states 'If absent (default): compute but DO NOT send' — this is correct behavior but misleadingly phrased. 'ENABLED flag absent' normally means feature disabled, but here it means feature partially runs (computes without sending). An implementer reading casually may invert the conditional.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite to be explicit: 'ENABLED flag absent = gate CLOSED (default). ENABLED flag present = gate OPEN (sends to Discord).'

findings.title: closed.json schema uses inconsistent version field naming (version vs schema_version)
findings.detail: self-heal-pipeline.md defines closed.json with 'version' field, rubric.json uses 'schema_version' and 'rubric_version', scan files have no schema_version. Three conventions for the same system create migration ambiguity.
findings.fix_sketch: Standardize on 'schema_version' (integer) across all data files. Document that 'rubric_version' is for the rubric document, 'schema_version' for data formats.

findings.title: README Phase 2 marked 'shipped' but Codex CLI is not installed — Tiered chain will fail
findings.detail: README line 36 marks Phase 2 as '✅ shipped (file-level only)' but Codex CLI is not installed. The Tiered review chain defined in splittasks strict mode will fail at runtime.
findings.fix_sketch: Either install Codex CLI (fulfilling Phase 2 prerequisites), or change status to '🟡 file-level only — Codex CLI not installed, Tiered chain unavailable'.

findings.title: proposer-spec default watchlist lists repos that don't exist on disk
findings.detail: proposer-spec.md section 2 default watchlist includes voice-discovery, spec-template, weautomatehq.com — none currently exist. An implementation using these defaults will fail at file read.
findings.fix_sketch: Update default watchlist to realistic repos (IFleet, factory, PhillUp) or document that defaults must be replaced before deployment.

findings.title: plan.md includes 'reopened' status that no component implements
findings.detail: plan.md line 91 includes 'reopened' in the status enum, but self-heal-pipeline uses 'regression' for the same concept. The 'reopened' value is dead and creates confusion.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove 'reopened' from status enum or document when it would be used vs 'regression'.

findings.title: README Related section uses tilde paths that are not clickable links
findings.detail: README lines 305-308 use paths like ~/dev/ai-products/IFleet/ROADMAP.md which are not clickable in any markdown renderer.
findings.fix_sketch: Note these as local filesystem references, not clickable links, or replace with GitHub URLs.
